en: Then, having offered the *bali* oblation, one should [visualize] the five colors—white, yellow, red, green, and black—produced from the five seed-syllables (*vaṃ*, *laṃ*, *raṃ*, *yaṃ*, *haṃ*), respectively arising from moonstone (*candrakānta*), topaz (*karketana*), ruby (*padmarāga*), emerald (*marakata*), and sapphire (*indranīla*), or else produced from pearl, gold, coral, and *miśrarājāvarta* (or *miśra* here refers to the four starting with pearl), or produced from minerals, or produced from *śāli* rice.

Having meditated upon auspicious materials—either flowers as appropriate, or those consecrated with powdered bricks, charcoal, animal parts, and so forth—as being the very nature of Vairocana and the other [Buddhas] produced from *vuṃ*, *āṃ*, *hrīḥ*, *khaṃ*, and *hūṃ*; and having brought them to a state of oneness with the rays of wisdom produced from *vuṃ* and the others, which have been drawn in and entered through the blazing gaze described in the ritual for preparing the thread, having entered the hearts of all the Tathāgatas situated in the sky; and having empowered them with the mantra *oṃ vuṃ* etc., one should recite the mantra *oṃ vajracitra samaya hūṃ* one hundred and eight times.

One should recite [the mantra]. Likewise, while stimulating them with a blazing gaze, one should place the syllable *hī* upon each [particle] and cause the dust to ignite through the empowerment of truth (*satyādhiṣṭhāna*), saying: "By that truth through which sentient beings and the Blessed Buddhas are impassioned by passion for sentient beings, by that truth may the dust blaze!"

Then, having offered the *bali*, [one visualizes] the white, yellow, red, green, and black colors produced from the seed-syllables BAṂ, LAṂ, RAṂ, YAṂ, and HAṂ, respectively, as being like moon-crystal, *karketana* ruby, and *padmarāga* ruby.

Those made from *aindra-nīla* gems, or those made from *mūṣāra-galva* mixed with pearls, gold, and coral—here, "mixed" refers to these four, beginning with pearls—or else those made from minerals, or made from fruit, or made from flowers; or, as appropriate, even with the powder of charcoal, brick, bone, and so forth.
Having visualized the consorts who have been properly assembled as being in the nature of Vairocana and the other [Buddhas], produced from the syllables BHRŪṂ, ĀṂ, HRĪṂ, KHAṂ, and HŪṂ;

Having summoned all the Tathāgatas arrayed in space by means of the blazing gaze—which is described as the activity of the *sūtra*-string composed of the wisdom pigments produced from *bhrūṃ* and so forth at their hearts—and having applied it, those [pigments] become of one taste with the wisdom pigments; they are then highly praised with *phrūṃ* and so forth.
One recites the mantra *oṃ vajracitra samaya hūṃ* one hundred and eight times. Likewise, generating brilliance through the "blazing gaze," one arranges the syllable *hīḥ* upon each [of the objects].

"By that truth through which sentient beings are [like] many particles of colored powder, and the Blessed Buddhas do not become attached to sentient beings due to attachment—by that truth, may these particles of colored powder blaze! Thus, one should ignite them through the blessing of truth (*satyādhiṣṭhāna*).
Through the excellence of the practice of the deity, they blaze. Having worshipped them with incense, flowers, and so forth, one should place them in a new vessel.
For one who has reached the excellence of deity meditation, [the mantra] will blaze forth. If one worships with incense, flowers, and so forth, it should be placed in a new vessel.
This is the procedure for the colored powder recitation (raṅgajāpavidhi). Oṃ.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the recitation of the colored powder mandala.
